repository.name: @webex/http-core
repository.purpose: Promise-based core HTTP client for the Cisco Webex JS SDK: request execution through an interceptor pipeline, interchangeable Node and browser transports, an HTTP status to error-class taxonomy, upload/download progress events, and buffer file-type detection.

commands.build: [NEEDS HUMAN INPUT] -- no committed command runs the build and its tests together; `build` delegates to `build:src` (compile only) and `test` chains the style/unit/integration/browser tiers without building. Absence confirmed by the repository owner during bootstrap.

glossary.definition: An object with any of onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError, folded over each request in both directions.
glossary.notes: Base class at src/lib/interceptor.js; the fold lives in src/request/utils.ts.

glossary.definition: The platform-specific function that performs network I/O.
glossary.notes: One of src/request/request.js or src/request/request.shim.js, selected by the browser field in package.json.

glossary.definition: The package's normalized representation of a transport, network, or CORS failure.
glossary.notes: Not an HTTP status; maps to NetworkOrCORSError.

glossary.definition: An HttpError descendant selected from a status code by select().
glossary.notes: An unmapped status falls back to the category default, such as 400 for an unmapped 4xx.

glossary.definition: A curried client factory that returns a new request function with the given options merged underneath per-call options.

evidence_rules.requirement: The script key must exist in package.json and must be addressed through the yarn workspace form naming @webex/http-core.
evidence_rules.notes: No command runs the build and its tests together.

evidence_rules.requirement: The file must exist under src/ as written, including its extension.
evidence_rules.notes: src/request/utils.ts is the only TypeScript source.

evidence_rules.requirement: Cite a source file and, where one exists, a test that invokes or observes the behavior.
evidence_rules.notes: Commit history is not acceptable evidence for this repository.

evidence_rules.requirement: Resolve every placeholder against a real repository value before emitting it.
evidence_rules.notes: Resolve against package.json or the source file; never emit a bracketed token.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not cite commit messages or pull requests as rationale.
negative_guidance.why: History for this path begins at the 2022 workspace migration while the code predates it, so it cannot explain why current behavior exists.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not assume a 404 always fails.
negative_guidance.why: src/interceptors/http-status.js resolves two redirect body shapes as successes.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat a resolved promise as a successful request.
negative_guidance.why: Transports resolve a statusCode 0 response for network failures instead of rejecting.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not change one transport without the other.
negative_guidance.why: package.json swaps them at build time, so divergence is invisible on the platform you are testing.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: The repository owner confirmed no coverage gate applies; the shared Jest config sets collectCoverage false.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not reformat src/lib/xhr.js to repository style.
negative_guidance.why: It is a vendored fork deliberately held close to upstream, with a whole-file eslint-disable.

high.expectation: A source file and a test both support the claim.

medium.expectation: Source supports the claim but no test does; state the gap rather than implying coverage.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle it; record a gap and ask rather than inferring.

rules: Orient before detailing: say what the module owns and what it does not before describing internals.
Cite a repository-relative file path for every claim.
Keep behavior owned by a sub-module in that sub-module's document and reference it by contract.
folder_readme_contract.example_policy: Include an example only when it is copied from a test or source file that exists.
folder_readme_contract.fallback: When neither source nor tests settle a question, record it as a gap instead of writing prose that implies coverage.

regression_feedback_rules.trigger: A defect appears on one platform because only one transport was changed.
required_followups: Mirror the fix in the sibling transport
Add a test on the previously uncovered side
Record the parity requirement in src/request/docs/README.md
regression_feedback_rules.notes: This is the package's most likely defect class.

regression_feedback_rules.trigger: A consumer breaks on an HttpError subtype change.
required_followups: Restore the subtype name and parent
Add a regression test in test/integration/spec/http-error.js
Treat the change as breaking in release notes
regression_feedback_rules.notes: Subtype identity is a published contract.

surface_owners.edit_boundary: src/index.js and the files it re-exports; changes are breaking for six sibling packages.
src/request; both transports must change together.
src/lib/xhr.js; port upstream changes as discrete diffs and do not reformat.

surface_owners.surface: shared build, lint, and test configuration
surface_owners.edit_boundary: Change upstream in the workspace config packages, not in the local passthrough files.

fallback_rules: When a command is not in package.json, stop and ask rather than inventing one.
When only one transport's behavior is known, state the platform explicitly instead of generalizing.
When rationale is not in the code or tests, record a gap; commit history is not a substitute.
When a change touches both transports, run the unit, integration, and browser tiers before reporting done.
